\chapter{Chapter03 — Decision Trees}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter03.SubspacesAndDecisionTrees.DecisionTrees
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.SubspacesAndDecisionTrees.DecisionTrees}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Binary decision trees]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
\leanok
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001
}
For a natural number $n$, a type $\alpha$, and a set $A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ of
available coordinates, a binary decision tree with available coordinates $A$ is either a
leaf labeled by an element of $\alpha$, or a query at some coordinate $i\in A$ with two
child trees, each having available coordinates $A\setminus\{i\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decision tree on all coordinates]
\lean{FABL.DecisionTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001
}
\label{FABL.DecisionTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
For a natural number $n$ and a type $\alpha$, a decision tree on all coordinates is a
binary decision tree whose initial set of available coordinates is $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Evaluation of a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001
}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let
$A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be the available coordinates. Evaluating a decision tree
with available coordinates $A$ at an input $x\in(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n$ returns the
leaf label if the tree is a leaf; at a query of coordinate $i$, it evaluates the
zero-child tree when $x_i=0$ and the one-child tree otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Number of leaves in a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b002}
A binary decision tree has one leaf if it terminates immediately; if it queries a
coordinate, its number of leaves is the sum of the numbers of leaves in its two
subtrees.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Depth of a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001
}
A binary decision tree that terminates immediately has depth $0$. If it queries a
coordinate, its depth is one plus the greater of the depths of its two subtrees.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Depth bounded by available coordinates]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth_le_card_available}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b002}
\difficulty{4}
For any finite set of available coordinates and any binary decision tree on those
coordinates, its depth is at most the number of available coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Depth bounded by dimension]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth_le_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth_le_card_available}
\difficulty{1}
For any natural number $n$ and any binary decision tree on all $n$ coordinates, its
depth is at most $n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on a finite set of coordinates. Its number of leaves is at
most $2^{\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Truncation of a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.truncate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p087-b008}
Given a binary decision tree, a fallback value, and a natural-number cutoff, truncation
leaves terminal outputs unchanged. At cutoff $0$, each query is replaced by a leaf
returning the fallback value; at a positive cutoff, the query is retained and both
subtrees are truncated at one less than the cutoff.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Depth bound after truncation]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth_truncate_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.truncate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a finite set of coordinates and let $T$ be a binary decision tree whose
leaves carry values in a type $\alpha$ and whose queries use coordinates from $A$, with
each queried coordinate removed from the set available to its descendants. For any
fallback value $a \in \alpha$ and any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, replacing each query reached
when the remaining truncation parameter is zero by a leaf carrying $a$ produces a tree
of depth at most $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a truncated tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_truncate_eq_eval_or_eq_fallback}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.truncate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$
coordinates with outputs in $\alpha$, let $a\in\alpha$ be a fallback value, let
$k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. The evaluation of $T$ truncated at
depth $k$ is either the evaluation of $T$ at $x$ or the fallback value $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Complete tree from a partial input]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTreeAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree}
Given a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to a set of outputs, a partial
input, and a set of available coordinates, recursively construct a decision tree as
follows: if any coordinates remain available, query the least one, and continue on the
two branches after setting that coordinate to $0$ or $1$ and removing it from the
available set. If none remain, make a leaf labelled by the value of the function at the
current input.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complete decision tree of a function]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTreeAux}
For a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to a set of outputs, construct the
decision tree that starts with every coordinate available and the all-zero input,
querying the least available coordinate at each step and branching on its two possible
values; each terminal leaf is labelled by the function value at the resulting input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the partial complete tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_completeTreeAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTreeAux, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\alpha$,
and let $p,x\in\{0,1\}^n$. For a set $I$ of coordinates, suppose $p$ and $x$ agree at
every coordinate outside $I$. Then the tree constructed from $f$ with partial input $p$
and available coordinates $I$ evaluates at $x$ to $f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the complete decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_completeTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_completeTreeAux}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let
$f:\{0,1\}^n\to\alpha$. The complete decision tree constructed from $f$, which queries
all coordinates, evaluates to $f$; that is, its evaluation as a function on the Boolean
cube equals $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[A decision tree computes a function]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b003
}
A binary decision tree with outputs in a type $\alpha$ computes a function from
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ to $\alpha$ when its evaluation agrees with that function on every
input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise Characterization of Computation]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.computes_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $T$
be a binary decision tree with available coordinates $A$, and let $f:\mathbb
F_2^n\to\alpha$. The tree computes $f$ if and only if, for every input $x\in\mathbb
F_2^n$, its evaluation at $x$ equals $f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness of the constructed decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTree_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.completeTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_completeTree}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional
binary cube to $\alpha$. The recursively constructed complete decision tree for $f$
computes $f$ on every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decision-tree depth of a function]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeDepth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_computingTree_with_depth}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p087-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001
}
For a function $f\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\alpha$, its decision-tree depth is the least
natural number that is the depth of a decision tree computing $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decision-tree size of a function]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeSize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_computingTree_with_size}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p087-b004
}
For a function $f\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\alpha$, its decision-tree size is the least
natural number that is the size of a decision tree computing $f$.
\end{definition}

\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_computingTree_depth_eq_decisionTreeDepth}

\begin{theorem}[Tree attaining decision tree size]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_computingTree_leafCount_eq_decisionTreeSize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_computingTree_with_size, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount}
\difficulty{1}

any function. There is a decision tree on all $n$ coordinates that computes $f$ and
whose number of leaves equals the decision tree size of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Minimum decision tree size bound]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeSize_le_of_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_computingTree_with_size, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\alpha$, and let $T$ be a
decision tree that computes $f$. The minimum number of leaves among decision trees
computing $f$ is at most the number of leaves of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Path data]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003}
For a natural number $n$ and a type $\alpha$, a path consists of an assignment of either
no value or a value in $\mathbb{F}_2$ to each of the $n$ coordinates, together with an
output label in $\alpha$ at the terminal leaf.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Empty path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path}
For any value, define the empty path to assign no bit to any of the $n$ coordinates and
to have that value as its terminal output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Extending a path by a query]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.𝔽₂}
Given a path, a coordinate, and a bit, define the path obtained by assigning that bit at
the chosen coordinate while preserving all other coordinate assignments and the terminal
output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Support of a path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003}
For a path on $n$ coordinates, its support is the set of coordinates to which the path
assigns a value in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Path length]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003
}
For a path on $n$ binary coordinates, define its length to be the number of coordinates
assigned a bit along the path.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the path support]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.mem_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let a path on $n$ binary
coordinates have a partial assignment of bits. For every coordinate $i$, it belongs to
the path's support if and only if its assignment is defined.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Support of the empty path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\alpha$ be a type. For any $v\in\alpha$, the
path with terminal label $v$ and no assigned coordinates has empty support.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the empty path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty_length}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\alpha$ be a type. For any $v\in\alpha$, the
path with terminal label $v$ and no assigned coordinates has length $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output under a coordinate query]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery_output}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a path on the $n$-dimensional binary cube have any
terminal label, and choose a coordinate and a binary value. Updating the path to fix
that coordinate to the chosen value leaves its terminal label unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Support after an additional query]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.mem_support_withQuery_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let a path on $n$ binary
coordinates have a partial assignment of bits. If the path is extended by assigning any
bit value at coordinate $i$, then a coordinate $j$ belongs to the resulting support if
and only if $j=i$ or $j$ belonged to the original support.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Support after assigning a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support_withQuery}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.mem_support_withQuery_iff, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let a path on $n$ binary
coordinates have a partial assignment of bits. After assigning any bit value at
coordinate $i$, the resulting support is the union of the original support with $\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Path length after a new query]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length_withQuery_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support_withQuery, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ specify values at some
coordinates, and choose a coordinate it does not yet specify and a value in
$\mathbb{F}_2$. After adding that coordinate and value to the path, the number of
specified coordinates is the original number plus one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Inputs matching a path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003}
For a path on $n$ binary coordinates and an input $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, say that $x$
matches the path when, at every coordinate assigned a bit by the path, $x$ has that bit.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Path cylinder]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p088-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p088-b003
}
For a path on $n$ binary coordinates, define its cylinder to be the set of inputs in
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that match the path.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Path indicator]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder, FABL.setIndicator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003
}
For a path on $n$ binary coordinates, define its indicator on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ to equal
$1$ on the path's cylinder and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Every point matches the empty path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type, and choose a value in
$\alpha$. The path that specifies no coordinates and has that terminal label is matched
by every point of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Unqueried coordinates are unset]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.assignment_eq_none_of_not_mem_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.mem_support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path on the $n$ binary coordinates assign to
each coordinate either a field element of $br/	ext{?}$ or no value, with support
consisting of the coordinates assigned a value. Any coordinate outside the support is
assigned no value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Matching after an additional query]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_withQuery_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.assignment_eq_none_of_not_mem_support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let a path on $n$ binary
coordinates have a partial assignment of bits and a terminal output in $\alpha$. If
coordinate $i$ is not in the path's support, then for every binary vector $x$, the path
obtained by assigning the value $b$ at $i$ matches $x$ if and only if the original path
matches $x$ and $x_i=b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator on matching vectors]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_one_of_matches}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.setIndicator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on the binary cube $br^n$ assign to each
coordinate either no value or a value in $br/2br$, and let $x\in\bbr^n$ agree with
every value assigned by the path. Then the indicator of the set of vectors matching the
path takes the value $1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator Outside a Path Cylinder]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_zero_of_not_matches}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.setIndicator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on the binary cube of dimension $n$ specify
a value in $br/2br$ or leave unspecified at each coordinate, and let $x$ be a binary
vector that does not match the path. Then the indicator of the path's cylinder at $x$ is
$0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator after adding a query]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_withQuery}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_one_of_matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_zero_of_not_matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_withQuery_iff, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ specify values at some
coordinates, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ that it does not specify and a
value $b\in\mathbb{F}_2$. For every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the indicator of the set
agreeing with the path after adding the requirement $x_i=b$ equals the original
indicator at $x$ if $x_i=b$, and equals zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decision tree paths]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b004
}
For a decision tree on $n$ binary coordinates with available-coordinate set
$A\subseteq[n]$, define its list of paths recursively: a leaf contributes the single
empty path with its stored output; a query at an available coordinate contributes the
paths from the zero child extended by assigning $0$ at that coordinate, followed by the
paths from the one child extended by assigning $1$ there.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Paths generated by a leaf]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths_leaf}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.empty, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type of output labels, and let a leaf of
a binary decision tree return a value $a\in\alpha$ without querying any coordinate. The
list of paths generated by this leaf consists of the single path that specifies no
coordinates and has output $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Paths generated by a query node]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths_query}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type of output labels, and let a binary
decision tree query a coordinate belonging to its available set, with two child trees
indexed by the remaining available coordinates. The paths generated by the tree are the
paths from the zero child with value $0$ specified at the queried coordinate, followed
by the paths from the one child with value $1$ specified there.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type of output labels, and let a binary
decision tree on $n$ coordinates query only coordinates in its available set, removing
each queried coordinate from the set available to its children. Every coordinate
specified by a path in the tree's generated path list belongs to the tree's available
set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Paths and leaves have equal counts]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.length_paths_eq_leafCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\difficulty{4}
For every decision tree on a finite set of coordinates, the number of paths in its path
list equals its number of leaves.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicators after extending paths]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_withQuery_pathIndicators}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_withQuery, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery_output, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite list of paths, let $i$ be a coordinate absent from the support of
every path in $P$, let $b\in\mathbb{F}_2$, and let $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Extend each
path by assigning value $b$ at coordinate $i$. The sum of the extended paths' leaf
outputs times their cylinder indicators at $x$ equals the original sum of outputs times
cylinder indicators if $x_i=b$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a real-output decision tree whose
queries are restricted to a set $I$ of the $n$ coordinates. For every input
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the value of $T$ at $x$ equals the sum over its paths $P$ of $P$'s
output multiplied by the indicator that $x$ matches the coordinate values specified by
$P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Function-valued path indicator expansion]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_sum_pathIndicators_function}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_sum_pathIndicators, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b004}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a real-output decision tree whose
queries are restricted to a set $I$ of the $n$ coordinates. The evaluation function of
$T$ equals the function that assigns to each input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ the sum over all
paths $P$ of $T$ of $P$'s output multiplied by the indicator that $x$ matches the
coordinate values specified by $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decision tree as a sum of path indicators]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.computes_eq_sum_pathIndicators}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on the binary cube
$\\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with real-valued leaves, and let $f:\\mathbb{F}_2^n\\to\\mathbb{R}$ be
the function computed by $T$. For each path $P$ of $T$, write $a_P$ for its leaf output
and let $1_P(x)$ be $1$ if $x$ agrees with every coordinate assignment fixed along $P$,
and $0$ otherwise. Then, for every $x\\in\\mathbb{F}_2^n$, $f(x)=\\sum_P a_P 1_P(x)$,
where the sum ranges over all paths of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output along a matching path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_path_output_of_mem_of_matches}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let $T$ be a decision tree
with outputs in $\alpha$ whose queries are restricted to a set $I$ of the $n$
coordinates. If a path $P$ occurs among the paths of $T$ and an input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$
matches every coordinate value specified by $P$, then evaluating $T$ at $x$ gives the
output recorded at the terminal leaf of $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Consistent path through a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_path_mem_and_matches}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let $T$ be a binary decision
tree on $n$ coordinates with output labels in $\alpha$. For every input
$x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$, some path in the list of paths of $T$ is consistent with $x$ at
every coordinate assigned along that path.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$
coordinates with outputs in $\alpha$, let $a\in\alpha$ be a fallback value, let
$k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. If the depth-$k$ truncation of $T$
evaluates differently from $T$ at $x$, then there is a path of $T$ matching $x$ whose
length is strictly greater than $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of a matching tree path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.path_eq_of_mem_of_matches}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_withQuery_iff, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.withQuery, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.path_support_subset_available, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths_leaf, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths_query, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type of output labels, and let a binary
decision tree on $n$ coordinates query only coordinates in a specified available set,
removing each queried coordinate from the set available to its children. If two paths in
the list of paths generated by the tree both agree with the same vector in $\mathbb
F_2^n$ at every coordinate they specify, then the two paths are equal.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$
coordinates with outputs in $\alpha$, and let $x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. There is exactly
one path in the list of paths of $T$ whose prescribed coordinate values all agree with
$x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output on a matched decision path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.computes_eq_path_output_of_matches}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on the binary cube $br^n$
with outputs in a type $\alpha$, and let $f:\bbr^n\to\alpha$ be the function computed by
$T$. If $P$ is one of the paths of $T$ and $x\in\bbr^n$ agrees with every coordinate
value assigned along $P$, then $f(x)$ equals the output label at the terminal leaf of
$P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b004}
For a finite set $S\subseteq[n]$, define the linear map from $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ to the
space of functions $S\to\mathbb{F}_2$ that sends each vector to its restriction to the
coordinates in $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate zero subspace]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction, FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b004}
For a finite set $S\subseteq[n]$, define the coordinate zero subspace of
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ to consist of the vectors that vanish at every coordinate in $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the coordinate zero subspace]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.mem_coordinateZeroSubspace_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $C$ be a set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $x$
be a point of the $n$-coordinate vector space over $\mathbb F_2$. Then $x$ belongs to
the kernel of restriction to $C$ if and only if $x_i=0$ for every $i\in C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Surjectivity of coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction_surjective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $S$ be any set of coordinates in
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Restricting a vector in $\mathbb F_2^n$ to the coordinates in $S$
defines a surjective linear map from $\mathbb F_2^n$ to the space of functions
$S\to\mathbb F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Codimension of a coordinate-zero subspace]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂Codimension_coordinateZeroSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateRestriction_surjective, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.finrank_perpendicularSubspace, FABL.f₂Codimension, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a set of coordinates among $n$ coordinates.
The dimension of the orthogonal complement, under the standard dot product over
$\mathbb{F}_2$, of the subspace of vectors vanishing on every coordinate in $S$ is
$|S|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Binary unit vector]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂UnitVector}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$ and a coordinate $j$ among the $n$ coordinates, define the
binary unit vector at $j$ to have value $1$ at coordinate $j$ and value $0$ at every
other coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unit vector at its own coordinate]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂UnitVector_apply_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂UnitVector}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $i$ be one of the $n$ coordinates. The unit vector
supported at $i$ has value $1$ at coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dot product with a coordinate unit vector]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂DotProduct_f₂UnitVector}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂UnitVector, FABL.f₂DotProduct}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$, and let $i$ be one of the $n$
coordinates. The dot product of $x$ with the unit vector supported at $i$ is $x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Support of an orthogonal vector]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂Support_subset_of_mem_perpendicular_coordinateZeroSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂DotProduct_f₂UnitVector, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂UnitVector, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.mem_coordinateZeroSubspace_iff, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.mem_f₂Support, FABL.mem_perpendicularSubspace_iff, FABL.perpendicularSubspace}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a set of coordinates among $n$ coordinates, and
let $\gamma\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ be orthogonal under the standard dot product to every
vector that vanishes on $S$. Then every coordinate where $\gamma$ is nonzero belongs to
$S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate subcube]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateSubcube}
\leanok
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p088-b001
}
For a finite set $S\subseteq[n]$ and a base point $b\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, define the
coordinate subcube to be the set of vectors $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that $x_i=b_i$ for
every $i\in S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in a coordinate subcube]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.mem_coordinateSubcube}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateSubcube}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b003}
\proofstep

  {direct}

\proofstep

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\proofstep

\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $C$ be a set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$b,x$ be points of the $n$-coordinate binary cube. Then $x$ belongs to the coordinate
subcube determined by $C$ and $b$ if and only if $x_i=b_i$ for every $i\in C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Path base assignment]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path}
For a path on $n$ coordinates with values in a set $\alpha$, define its base vector by
taking the assigned binary value at each coordinate, and taking $0$ wherever the path
has no assigned value.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of points matching a path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_iff_forall_mem_support_eq_base}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.mem_support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ specify values at some
coordinates, and let $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The point $x$ agrees with every value
specified by the path if and only if, at every coordinate specified by the path, $x$
equals the point that uses the path's assigned value there and $0$ at every unspecified
coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The base point matches the path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_base}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_iff_forall_mem_support_eq_base}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ specify values at
some coordinates. The point whose value at each specified coordinate is the path's
assigned value, and whose value at every unspecified coordinate is $0$, agrees with
every value specified by the path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Path cylinders as coordinate subcubes]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder_eq_coordinateSubcube}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_iff_forall_mem_support_eq_base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateSubcube}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003
}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path assign either no value or a value in
$br/2br$ to each of the $n$ coordinates. Its cylinder—the set of binary vectors
agreeing with every assigned value—is exactly the coordinate subcube that fixes the
path’s support coordinates to the vector obtained by using each assigned value and using
$0$ at every unassigned coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A path cylinder is an affine subspace]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder_eq_binaryAffineSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_iff_forall_mem_support_eq_base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.mem_coordinateZeroSubspace_iff, FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.mem_binaryAffineSubspace_iff_add_mem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $P$ be a path on the $n$ binary coordinates.
The set of binary vectors agreeing with all values fixed by $P$ is the affine subspace
consisting of the path's base vector plus the subspace of vectors that vanish on every
coordinate fixed by $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Codimension equals path length]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.codimension_coordinateZeroSubspace_eq_length}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂Codimension_coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.f₂Codimension}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $P$ be a path on the $n$ coordinates, with
length equal to the number of coordinates fixed by the path. In the vector space of
binary vectors of length $n$, the codimension of the subspace of vectors that vanish on
every coordinate fixed by $P$ equals the length of $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Path indicator as an affine-subspace indicator]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_binaryAffineSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.cylinder_eq_binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.setIndicator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let a path on $br^n$ over the binary field assign
either no value or a binary value to each coordinate. Its cylinder is the set of binary
vectors agreeing with every assigned value; its support consists of the coordinates with
assigned values, and its base vector records those values and is $0$ elsewhere. The
indicator function of the cylinder equals the indicator function of the translate, by
this base vector, of the subspace of vectors that vanish on the support.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Inverse path size]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length}
For a path of length $\ell$, define its inverse path size to be $2^{-\ell}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reciprocal size of the orthogonal complement]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePerpendicularCard_coordinateZeroSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.codimension_coordinateZeroSubspace_eq_length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ specify values at
some coordinates. The reciprocal of $2$ raised to the dimension of the orthogonal
complement, under the standard dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$, of the subspace of
vectors vanishing on those coordinates equals $2^{-k}$, where $k$ is the number of
coordinates specified by the path.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let a path on the binary cube
of dimension $n$ have output in $\alpha$. The spectral sparsity of the indicator of the
set of binary vectors matching the path is $2^\ell$, where $\ell$ is the number of
coordinates in the path's support.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral one-norm of a path indicator]

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b003}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, and let a path on the binary cube
of dimension $n$ have output in $\alpha$. The spectral $1$-norm of the indicator of the
set of binary vectors matching the path is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ specify values at
some coordinates. Regard its indicator as a function on the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ via
the coordinatewise bijection that sends $0$ to $1$ and $1$ to $-1$. Every Fourier
coefficient of this function, indexed by a subset of coordinates, is an integer multiple
of $2^{-k}$, where $k$ is the number of coordinates specified by the path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier degree of a path indicator]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.vectorFourierDegree_indicator_le_length}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.f₂Support_subset_of_mem_perpendicular_coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_ne_zero_iff, FABL.vectorFourierDegree, FABL.vectorFourierDegree_le_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let a path on the $n$-dimensional binary cube fix some
coordinates. The Fourier degree of the indicator of the set of inputs matching those
fixed coordinates is at most the number of coordinates fixed by the path.
\end{theorem}
